I am a PhD candidate at the Utrecht University School of Economics, supervised
by Inge van den Bijgaart and Jacob A. Jordaan. My dissertation is on climate
policy design for household decarbonisation.

I work on the design and evaluation of climate policy, and in particular on who
gains from the instruments meant to decarbonise households, and at what public
cost. Most of my current research combines Dutch administrative microdata from
Statistics Netherlands (CBS) with quasi-experimental designs to evaluate the
effects of subsidies and financing instruments for household decarbonisation.

Before starting my PhD I completed an MSc in Environmental Economics at the
University of Turin and a BSc in Economics at Sapienza University of Rome. In
autumn 2025 I visited the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research and TU
Berlin, hosted by Linus Mattauch.

At Utrecht I teach econometrics and macroeconomics, and supervise bachelor's
theses.

## Research interests

- Environmental and energy economics
- Policies for household decarbonisation
- Public economics and policy evaluation
- Distributional and efficiency effects of policy mixes
- Applied microeconometrics
